newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GIO interested in Australia's Trust Bank.
newsitem.headline: GIO interested in Australia's Trust Bank.

text.p: GIO Australia Ltd said on Friday it would be interested in acquiring Australia's Trust Bank but as yet had not seen the bank's sale terms.
"Anything that is in financial services that has a client base we are interested in - but I haven't seen the terms on which it might be for sale," GIO's managing director Bill Jocelyn told Reuters.
Tasmanian-based Trust Bank announced in March that it was looking for a strategic partner to take a 49 percent stake, hopefully by early next year.
The bank then plans to issue 41 percent of its equity to the public by the end of 1998 and embark on national expansion.
Paul Kemp, Trust Bank's managing director, earlier told Reuters a listed insurer and two offshore institutions had expressed interest in buying the stake.
Jocelyn said he believed obtaining Trust Bank's client base would be the most attractive feature for GIO or any other interested buyer.
Bank licences were no longer important following the Wallis inquiry into Australia's financial system, Jocelyn said.
"If anything Trust Bank will be of interest because of their management, their business and their client base," he said.
Trust Bank has net assets of A$143 million, implying a total value of A$257 million, based on the goodwill paid in the sale of another regional bank, BankWest Ltd, in 1995.
The bank has ruled out any other local banks as a strategic partner, saying none of them would be interested in fulfilling Trust Bank's broader ambitions.
